cov_intro: What Fontes reaches in each jurisdiction: its courts and types of legislation, each marked reached or not; the sources and their terms; and what Fontes does not reach, and why. Counts read reached + partly½ / all rows, so `5+1½/8` means 5 rows reached and 1 partly reached, out of 8. Generated by `scripts/catalogue.py`; do not edit by hand.
cov_reliability: **How reliable the court lists are.** Whether each row is reached comes from reading the adapter code. The court and legislation lists themselves were drafted by AI agents from their own knowledge, checked against an official page where one could be opened. Many official judiciary sites were blocked or unreachable, so a listed reference does not always mean the page was read. Countries marked UNVERIFIED had no official source at all. Treat the lists as a draft to check, not an authority.
cov_last_column: **The last column** says, for anything Fontes does not fully reach, whether it can be reached at all: 🟢 available (an official or licensed source publishes it; Fontes has not built it), 🔒 blocked (a source exists but robots.txt, terms, a bot wall, a login or a paywall stops us), ⚫ offline (checked: not published online), ❓ unknown. Each entry says what it rests on: 'fetched <date>' means the page was opened that day; 'search result only' is weaker. Sites that time out from the UK are marked unknown or blocked with a note; geo-blocking is not proven.
cov_counts: {adapters} adapters; {missing} UN member states without one.
cov_scorecard_intro: A jurisdiction counts as covered when Fontes reaches at least one of two areas completely: the precedents of its top general court (the Yargıtay equivalent), or its constitution and primary acts (kanun level and above). Secondary legislation and lower courts do not count. ✅ complete (minor gaps noted), ◐ gap (something published is missing, or the source is off until permission), ❌ none. Judgement calls are in research/scorecard_overrides.json.
